scope: The advantage chain from the 1947 transistor to the 2026 AI economy.

facts.claim: Bell Laboratories' John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley invented the transistor in 1947.
quotes: In 1947, the transistor, arguably the most important invention developed by Bell Laboratories, was invented by John Bardeen, Walter Houser Brattain, and William Bradford Shockley (who subsequently shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956).

facts.claim: The 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics went jointly to Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain for the transistor effect.
quotes: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1956 was awarded jointly to William Bradford Shockley, John Bardeen and Walter Houser Brattain "for their researches on semiconductors and their discovery of the transistor effect"

facts.claim: Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory was founded by William Shockley in 1955 with funding from Beckman Instruments.
quotes: Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory, later known as Shockley Transistor Corporation, was a pioneering semiconductor developer founded by William Shockley, and funded by Beckman Instruments, Inc., in 1955.

facts.claim: Eight Shockley Semiconductor engineers left to start their own company.
quotes: The eight who left Shockley Semiconductor were Julius Blank, Victor Grinich, Jean Hoerni, Eugene Kleiner, Jay Last, Gordon Moore, Robert Noyce, and Sheldon Roberts.

facts.claim: The eight formed Fairchild Semiconductor on 18 September 1957 after agreeing terms with Sherman Fairchild in August.
quotes: In August 1957, they reached an agreement with Sherman Fairchild, and on September 18, 1957, they formed Fairchild Semiconductor.

facts.claim: By 1960 Fairchild was an incubator of Silicon Valley whose alumni created dozens of corporations, including Intel and AMD.
quotes: In 1960, it became an incubator of Silicon Valley and was directly or indirectly involved in the creation of dozens of corporations, including Intel and AMD.

facts.claim: Fairchild developed the planar process in 1959.
quotes: The planar process was developed at Fairchild Semiconductor in 1959 and it proved to be one of the most important single advances in semiconductor technology.

facts.claim: Shockley circulated the Bell Labs passivation preprint to his senior staff, including Jean Hoerni, in December 1956.
quotes: At Shockley Semiconductor, Shockley had circulated the preprint of their article in December 1956 to all his senior staff, including Jean Hoerni.
facts.notes: Hoerni then proposed oxide-protected transistors; the passivation discovery itself was Frosch and Derick at Bell Labs in 1955.

facts.claim: Robert Noyce invented the first monolithic integrated circuit in 1959.
quotes: Robert Noyce invented the first monolithic integrated circuit in 1959.

facts.claim: Jack Kilby won the 2000 Nobel Prize in physics for his part in the invention of the integrated circuit.
quotes: Kilby won the 2000 Nobel Prize in physics for his part in the invention of the integrated circuit.

facts.claim: Fairchild's first batch of 100 devices was sold to IBM at $150 apiece for the B-70 bomber's computer.
quotes: The first batch of 100 was sold to IBM for $150 apiece in order to build the computer for the B-70 bomber.

facts.claim: Intel was founded in 1968 by Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce with investor Arthur Rock.
quotes: Intel was founded in 1968 by engineers Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce, along with investor Arthur Rock, and is associated with the executive leadership and vision of Andrew Grove.

facts.claim: Federico Faggin left Fairchild for Intel in 1970 to design the first microprocessors.
quotes: Federico Faggin, frustrated, left Fairchild to join Intel in 1970 and design the first microprocessors using SGT.

facts.claim: Intel's 1103, released in 1970, was the first commercially available DRAM.
quotes: The three-transistor cell implemented in the first commercially available dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), the 1103 released in 1970, solved these issues.

facts.claim: The 1103 was the world's bestselling semiconductor memory chip by 1972.
quotes: The 1103 was the bestselling semiconductor memory chip in the world by 1972, as it replaced core memory in many applications.

facts.claim: Intel introduced the 4004 microprocessor in 1971, built for Busicom, but it did not become Intel's core business until the mid-1980s.
quotes: Originally developed for the Japanese company Busicom to replace a number of ASICs in a calculator already produced by Busicom, the Intel 4004 was introduced to the mass market on November 15, 1971, though the microprocessor did not become the core of Intel's business until the mid-1980s.

facts.claim: In 1983 Japanese memory makers squeezed Intel's profits and Andy Grove refocused Intel on microprocessors.
quotes: In 1983, at the dawn of the personal computer era, Intel's profits came under increased pressure from Japanese memory-chip manufacturers, and then-president Andy Grove focused the company on microprocessors.
facts.notes: The brief dates the exit to 1985; the page says Grove closed much of the DRAM business 'during this period' without a precise year.

facts.claim: The IBM PC, released 12 August 1981, used an Intel 8088 processor.
quotes: Powered by an x86-architecture Intel 8088 processor, the machine was based on open architecture and third-party peripherals.
Released August 12, 1981; 45 years ago (1981-08-12)

facts.claim: Compaq, the first IBM PC clone maker, shipped the first 80386-based system in 1986, beating IBM and making Intel a key component supplier.
quotes: Compaq, the first IBM PC "clone" manufacturer, produced a desktop system based on the faster 80286 processor in 1985 and in 1986 quickly followed with the first 80386-based system, beating IBM and establishing a competitive market for PC-compatible systems and setting up Intel as a key component supplier.

facts.claim: TSMC was established in 1987 as a joint venture of Taiwan's government, ITRI and private investors, and became the world's first dedicated foundry.
quotes: TSMC was established in 1987 as a joint venture between Taiwan's government, the Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), and private investors.
Morris Chang founded the company to commercialise semiconductor research originally developed at ITRI, becoming the world's first dedicated semiconductor foundry.

facts.claim: TSMC holds approximately 70% of the global foundry market.
quotes: It holds a commanding majority in the semiconductor foundry market, accounting for approximately 70% of the global market share.

facts.claim: TSMC was the first foundry to commercialise ASML's EUV lithography in high volume.
quotes: TSMC was the first foundry to market 7-nanometre and 5-nanometre (used by the 2020 Apple A14 and M1 SoCs, the MediaTek Dimensity 8100, and AMD Ryzen 7000 series processors) production capabilities, and the first to commercialise ASML's extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography technology in high volume.
facts.notes: No year in the quote; value 0 is a flag.

facts.claim: Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
quotes: Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia has been described as a Big Tech company and is among the largest companies by market capitalization.

facts.claim: Sega's Shoichiro Irimajiri persuaded Sega to invest $5 million in Nvidia after Nvidia had failed to deliver on its contract.
quotes: However, Irimajiri believed in Nvidia's potential and persuaded Sega's management to invest $5 million into the company.
Investing in Nvidia after it had already failed to deliver on its contract turned out to be Irimajiri's best decision as Sega's president.

facts.claim: Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million after 2000.
quotes: After Irimajiri left Sega in 2000, Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million.

facts.claim: Nvidia went public on 22 January 1999.
quotes: Nvidia went public on January 22, 1999.

facts.claim: In late 1999 Nvidia released the GeForce 256, its first product marketed as a GPU.
quotes: In late 1999, Nvidia released the GeForce 256 (NV10), its first product expressly marketed as a GPU, which was most notable for introducing onboard transformation and lighting (T&L) to consumer-level 3D hardware.

facts.claim: In December 2000 Nvidia agreed to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival 3dfx.
quotes: In December 2000, Nvidia reached an agreement to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival 3dfx, a pioneer in consumer 3D graphics technology leading the field from the mid-1990s until 2000.

facts.claim: CUDA was created in 2004 and officially released in 2007.
quotes: CUDA was created in 2004 and was officially released in 2007.

facts.claim: AlexNet was trained for five to six days on two Nvidia GTX 580 GPUs and won the 2012 ImageNet competition.
quotes: The model was trained for 90 epochs over a period of five to six days using two Nvidia GTX 580 GPUs (3GB each).
During 2012, Krizhevsky performed hyperparameter optimization on the network until it won the ImageNet competition later the same year.

facts.claim: Each GTX 580 was priced at US$500 on release.
quotes: These GPUs have a theoretical performance of 1.581 TFLOPS in float32 and were priced at US$500 upon release.

facts.claim: Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016, cutting a training run from six days to two hours.
quotes: Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016 to help it train larger and more complex AI models with the capability of reducing processing time from six days to two hours.

facts.claim: Nvidia announced on 11 March 2019 that it would acquire Mellanox for $6.9 billion.
quotes: On March 11, 2019, Nvidia announced its intent to acquire the company for $6.9 billion.

facts.claim: The Transformer, based solely on attention, was submitted to arXiv on 12 June 2017.
quotes: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
Submitted on 12 Jun 2017
facts.notes: Authors at Google, per the Wikipedia transformer article (lineage-transformer-google-2017).

facts.claim: The Transformer reached 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French after 3.5 days on eight GPUs.
quotes: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature.

facts.claim: The original transformer architecture was proposed in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by researchers at Google.
quotes: The original version of the transformer architecture was proposed in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" by researchers at Google.

facts.claim: Kaplan et al. found language-model loss scales as a power law in model size, data and compute over more than seven orders of magnitude (submitted 23 January 2020).
quotes: The loss scales as a power-law with model size, dataset size, and the amount of compute used for training, with some trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude.
Submitted on 23 Jan 2020

facts.claim: GPT-3 had 175 billion parameters, ten times any previous non-sparse language model (submitted 28 May 2020).
quotes: Specifically, we train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model, and test its performance in the few-shot setting.
Submitted on 28 May 2020

facts.claim: Eleven OpenAI employees left between December 2020 and January 2021 to establish Anthropic.
quotes: Eleven employees left OpenAI, mostly between December 2020 and January 2021, in order to establish Anthropic.

facts.claim: ChatGPT was released on 30 November 2022.
quotes: Originally released on November 30, 2022, the product uses large language models – specifically generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs) – to generate text, speech, and images in response to user prompts.

facts.claim: ChatGPT reached 100 million monthly users two months after release and 900 million weekly users in February 2026.
quotes: ChatGPT was quickly adopted, reaching 100 million monthly active users two months after its release and 900 million weekly active users in February 2026.

facts.claim: ASML began developing EUV lithography in 1997.
quotes: Meanwhile, in 1997, ASML began developing its EUV lithography technology.

facts.claim: In 2012 ASML sold 23 percent of itself to Intel, TSMC and Samsung.
quotes: To achieve this, ASML launched a co-investment program in 2012, under which 23 percent of the company was sold to its three largest customers: Intel, TSMC and Samsung.

facts.claim: Intel invested $4.1 billion in ASML in July 2012 for a 15 percent stake.
quotes: To help fund the expensive research and development required, Intel invested $4.1 billion in ASML in July 2012 in exchange for a 15 percent stake.

facts.claim: ASML is, as of 2026, the world's only manufacturer of EUV lithography machines.
quotes: It is the largest supplier to the semiconductor industry and, as of 2026[update] , the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are required to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips.

facts.claim: Nvidia took 180 days to go from $1 trillion to $2 trillion; Apple and Microsoft each took over 500.
quotes: Nvidia needed only 180 days to get to $2 trillion from $1 trillion, while the first two companies, Apple and Microsoft, each took over 500 days.

facts.claim: On 29 October 2025 Nvidia became the first company to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization.
quotes: On October 29, 2025, Nvidia became the first company to reach a market capitalization of $5 trillion.

facts.claim: NVIDIA's market capitalization in November 2026 was $4.506 trillion, the world's 2nd most valuable company by that data.
quotes: Market capitalization of NVIDIA (NVDA) Market cap: $4.506 Trillion USD As of November 2026
This makes NVIDIA the world's 2nd most valuable company by market cap according to our data.

facts.claim: As of Q1 2025 Nvidia held 92% of the discrete desktop and laptop GPU market.
quotes: As of the first quarter of 2025, Nvidia held a 92% share of the discrete desktop and laptop GPU market.
facts.period: Q1 2025 (market: discrete desktop and laptop GPUs, not AI accelerators)

facts.claim: In August 2025 the US government bought 433.3 million Intel shares at $20.47, a 9.9% stake.
quotes: In August 2025, the United States government purchased 433.3 million Intel shares at $20.47 per share, equivalent to a 9.9% stake.

facts.claim: The Hutter Prize, launched in 2006, rests on the organizers' belief that text compression and AI are equivalent problems.
quotes: Launched in 2006, the prize awards 5,000 euros for each one percent improvement
The organizers believe that text compression and AI are equivalent problems.
facts.notes: Supports the 'intelligence as compression' premise only as a position of the prize organizers, not a settled result.

facts.claim: Jensen Huang began as a microchip designer in Silicon Valley and chose AMD over Texas Instruments and LSI Logic.
quotes: He was approached for positions at Texas Instruments, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and LSI Logic,[30] ultimately choosing the California-based AMD due to already being familiar with the company.

actors.name: Bell Labs (AT&T)

triad.information: the physics and the passivation discovery

actors.advantage: A monopoly telephone company funded open-ended physics; the transistor came from that protected research budget, and its people and ideas then leaked outward.
actors.desire: a better amplifier than the vacuum tube for the phone network
actors.fear: being outflanked by others commercialising its invention

actors.name: Shockley Semiconductor
actors.role: the first Silicon Valley semiconductor firm; its talent walked out
actors.advantage: It gathered the best young semiconductor engineers but could not keep them: its founder's management drove eight of them out.

actors.name: Fairchild Semiconductor
actors.role: planar process and monolithic IC; the root of Silicon Valley

triad.information: the passivation idea, the planar insight
triad.environment: Cold-War orders and Sherman Fairchild's parent

actors.advantage: Silicon, the planar process and the monolithic integrated circuit gave it a manufacturable device that rivals could not yet make; early military and IBM orders paid for it. Its engineers then left to found dozens of firms.
actors.desire: to make silicon the standard and ICs cheap
actors.fear: its own people leaving with the know-how

actors.name: Texas Instruments
actors.advantage: Co-inventor of the integrated circuit (Kilby, 1958), but its version was not monolithic and was harder to manufacture at scale.
actors.fear: being the second source of a better process

actors.name: Intel
actors.role: memory pioneer turned x86 monopolist, now US-state-supported
actors.advantage: Intel moved from DRAM to the microprocessor, and the IBM PC and its clones made x86 the standard; software lock-in and fab scale held the position for decades until the foundry model beat its process lead.
actors.desire: a process lead and foundry business
actors.fear: irrelevance to AI and to leading-edge manufacturing

actors.name: TSMC
actors.role: the pure-play foundry that makes the world's leading-edge chips
actors.advantage: By manufacturing for everyone and competing with no customer, it let design-only firms exist; its volume funded the lead in each node and the first volume EUV production.
actors.fear: a Taiwan crisis or a customer building its own fab

actors.name: NVIDIA
actors.role: designs the GPUs that frontier AI is trained on

triad.environment: the gaming market that paid for it

actors.advantage: Three decades of GPU work for gamers produced a parallel chip and the CUDA software layer; when neural networks, then transformers, proved to run best on them, the gamers' installed base became the AI industry's default platform.
actors.desire: to be the platform for all accelerated computing
actors.fear: a cheaper chip or a model that no longer needs it

actors.name: ASML
actors.role: the only maker of EUV lithography machines
actors.advantage: Its customers funded and co-owned it: Intel, TSMC and Samsung bought 23 percent in 2012 to pay for EUV, which took from 1997 until the late 2010s to build.
actors.fear: a customer or a state replicating EUV

actors.name: OpenAI
actors.role: scaled the transformer into GPT-3 and ChatGPT
actors.advantage: It bet that scaling transformers on large compute would keep improving results, then shipped ChatGPT, the product that made the bet visible.

actors.name: Anthropic
actors.advantage: Its founders carried the scaling playbook out of OpenAI; the lineage is people, not patents.

actors.name: Google (Brain/DeepMind)
actors.advantage: It held the research that made the modern AI industry and published it, letting rivals build on it.

actors.name: IBM
actors.role: first big buyer of Fairchild devices; created the PC market with an open design
actors.advantage: first big buyer of Fairchild devices; created the PC market with an open design

actors.name: Compaq
actors.role: first IBM PC clone maker; shipped the first 80386 system
actors.advantage: first IBM PC clone maker; shipped the first 80386 system

actors.name: Sega
actors.role: early investor that kept Nvidia alive
actors.advantage: early investor that kept Nvidia alive

actors.name: 3dfx Interactive
actors.role: consumer 3D pioneer, bought by Nvidia for its assets
actors.advantage: consumer 3D pioneer, bought by Nvidia for its assets

actors.name: Mellanox Technologies
actors.role: networking bought by Nvidia for $6.9 billion
actors.advantage: networking bought by Nvidia for $6.9 billion

actors.name: AlexNet team (Toronto)
actors.role: showed deep nets on two gaming GPUs beat everything
actors.advantage: showed deep nets on two gaming GPUs beat everything

actors.role: states that compression and AI are equivalent problems
actors.advantage: states that compression and AI are equivalent problems

chokepoints.alternatives: none; development took from 1997 to the late 2010s

chokepoints.share: about 70% of the global foundry market
chokepoints.alternatives: Samsung and Intel are behind on volume

chokepoints.share: 92% of discrete desktop and laptop GPUs (Q1 2025); accelerator share is in the compute cluster

flashpoints.title: The eight leave Shockley
flashpoints.mechanism: A founder who could recruit but not manage lost his whole team, who took the technique with them.
flashpoints.outcome: Fairchild formed 18 Sept 1957; Shockley's firm was acquired by Clevite.

flashpoints.title: Planar monolithic IC against Kilby's version
flashpoints.mechanism: Photo-masked planar fabrication turned the IC from a lab result into a product.
flashpoints.outcome: Noyce's monolithic IC, 1959; Kilby later won the Nobel Prize.

flashpoints.title: Intel leaves DRAM for microprocessors
flashpoints.mechanism: When Japanese memory makers crushed DRAM margins, Intel moved its capital to the microprocessor that the PC market needed.
flashpoints.outcome: Grove closed much of the DRAM business; the 386 made Intel near-exclusive supplier.

flashpoints.title: The IBM PC adopts Intel
flashpoints.advantage: a standard set by an open design
flashpoints.mechanism: IBM's open architecture let clones copy the PC but not the chip, so the standard's value went to Intel and Microsoft.
flashpoints.outcome: Compaq's 1986 386 machine beat IBM to market and made Intel the key supplier.

flashpoints.title: The pure-play foundry
flashpoints.advantage: a foundry that competes with no customer
flashpoints.mechanism: By making chips for others, TSMC let designers without fabs exist and pooled their volume.
flashpoints.outcome: About 70% of the global foundry market today.

flashpoints.title: Nvidia buys 3dfx
flashpoints.mechanism: After the GeForce 256, the one-time leader in consumer 3D lost ground and sold its assets.
flashpoints.outcome: Nvidia agreed in Dec 2000 to acquire 3dfx's intellectual assets.

flashpoints.title: AlexNet on two gaming GPUs
flashpoints.advantage: parallel hardware already in the market
flashpoints.mechanism: A deep network trained in 5 to 6 days on two $500 GPUs beat every other ImageNet entry, showing that GPUs, not CPUs, were the engine of deep learning.
flashpoints.outcome: Won ImageNet 2012; CUDA (2007) was the ready software.

flashpoints.title: Attention Is All You Need
flashpoints.mechanism: Dropping recurrence let training spread across many GPUs, so scale became the lever; the paper was public.
flashpoints.outcome: 41.8 BLEU after 3.5 days on eight GPUs.

flashpoints.title: ChatGPT
flashpoints.advantage: betting on scale and shipping first
flashpoints.mechanism: OpenAI turned scaling laws and GPT-3 into a product the public could use.
flashpoints.outcome: 100 million monthly users in two months; 900 million weekly in February 2026.

flashpoints.title: Customers fund EUV
flashpoints.mechanism: Intel, TSMC and Samsung bought 23 percent of ASML in 2012 to underwrite EUV.
flashpoints.outcome: As of 2026 ASML is the only EUV maker.

flashpoints.title: Nvidia at the top
flashpoints.advantage: the platform the whole AI chain stands on
flashpoints.mechanism: Gaming, CUDA, AlexNet, the Transformer and scale all led to the same chip.
flashpoints.outcome: $4.5 trillion market cap, 2nd in the world; first to $5 trillion in 2025.
